grades.question: How is the Conflict deck built, and what happens to unused Conflict cards?
grades.expected: Shuffle all four III cards at the bottom, five randomly dealt of nine II cards above, one randomly dealt of three I cards on top: ten total. Return unused cards to the box without looking.

observed.answer: Shuffle all 4 III cards and place them face down at the bottom; shuffle 9 II and deal 5 face down above; shuffle 3 I and deal 1 face down on top. Return the unused I and II cards to the box unseen.
observed.evidence: Setup: face-down Conflict deck; unused cards returned unseen.

grades.reason: Builds the concealed 4 III/5 II/1 I deck with tier shuffling and unseen return of unused cards.

grades.question: What are the starting score, Agents, troops and water for a human in a four-player game versus a three-player game?
grades.expected: Four players start at 1 VP; three at 0. Each has two Agents on Leader and third beside board, three troops in garrison with remaining nine in supply, and one water.

observed.answer: Both player counts start at 0 VP in a three-player game and 1 VP in a four-player game. Each human starts with two Agents on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board; three troops in their garrison and nine in supply; and 1 water.
observed.evidence: Setup, step 6: Score track on 1 in 4P, otherwise 0; two Agents; three troops; 1 water.

grades.reason: Correctly distinguishes starting VP and gives both Agent locations, 3/9 troop split, and 1 water.

grades.question: Can you Reveal with Agents left, and can you later take an Agent turn in the same round? What cards supply Reveal effects and where do all played cards go?
grades.expected: May Reveal early; no more turns this phase after Reveal. Only cards remaining in hand and just revealed supply Reveal effects, not Agent-turn cards. Clean Up puts all Agent and Reveal cards in discard pile.

observed.answer: Yes, you may Reveal while Agents remain, but after Revealing your turns are skipped for the rest of Player Turns. Reveal effects come only from cards still in hand that you reveal, not cards used on Agent turns. At Clean Up, all cards in front of you from both kinds of turns go to your discard pile.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure: Agent turns optional; Reveal Cards/Effects/Clean Up.

grades.reason: Allows early Reveal, bars further Player Turns, limits Reveal effects to revealed hand, and discards both sets.

grades.question: May an Agent-turn card effect provide resources to pay the destination entry cost? How many Agents can one card send, and can a card without Agent icons be used?
grades.expected: Entry costs paid immediately before any card or space effects; cannot use later gains to pay entry. One card sends one Agent using one matching icon. No-icon card cannot be played on an Agent turn.

observed.answer: No: entry costs must be paid immediately before resolving effects from the destination or played Agent card. One card selects only one Agent icon and sends one Agent. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used for an Agent turn; it may be revealed.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure, Agent Turn: pay immediately; one icon/one Agent; no-icon cards only Reveal.

grades.reason: Requires entry resources before Agent-card/space gains, one Agent using one icon, and rejects no-icon Agent cards.

grades.question: At a Combat space you recruit three troops this turn and already have four garrisoned. How many can deploy? What if the destination is not a Combat space, and where do recruited troops originate?
grades.expected: May deploy all three newly recruited plus at most two older garrison troops, five total. Normal deployment unavailable at noncombat space. Recruit from own supply into garrison; empty supply prevents recruiting.

observed.answer: At a Combat space, deploy all three troops recruited this turn plus up to two from the four already in your garrison, for a maximum of five. At a non-Combat space, normal deployment is not permitted. Recruits come from your supply and enter your garrison before deployment.
observed.evidence: Actions—Recruiting & Deploying: recruited troops from supply; Combat space allows current-turn recruits plus up to two garrison units.

grades.reason: Gives maximum five deployment, no normal deployment off Combat spaces, and supply-to-garrison recruitment.

grades.question: How do you use a Spy Agent icon, Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence? Can the same Spy pay for both, and when must Gather Intelligence be chosen?
grades.expected: Spy Agent icon permits a connected space without recalling Spy. Infiltrate recalls own connected Spy to bypass another player Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls own connected Spy to draw, chosen immediately after placement before card/space effects. Same Spy cannot do both; separate Spies can.

observed.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to any space connected to an observation post where you currently have your Spy; you do not recall it. Infiltrate recalls a Spy at a connected post to bypass another player’s Agent, not your own. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy to draw a card, chosen immediately after placing your Agent and before any space/card effects. The same Spy cannot pay for both; two different Spies can be used for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence on the same placement.
observed.evidence: Special Rules—Spies: Spy Agent icon, Infiltrate, Gather Intelligence timing and distinct-Spy restriction.

grades.reason: Distinguishes all three Spy uses, separate recalls, other-player occupancy, and immediate Gather Intelligence timing.

grades.question: With two troops, one sandworm and four revealed swords, what is your strength? What if your final unit is removed? Can you participate in Combat Intrigue with no unit?
grades.expected: Strength 11 (2+2+3+4). No units means zero strength regardless swords. Without a unit cannot participate in Combat Intrigue.

observed.answer: Strength is 11: two troops = 4, one sandworm = 3, four swords = 4. If the final unit is removed, strength becomes 0. With no unit in the Conflict, you cannot play Combat Intrigue.
observed.evidence: Actions—Strength; Phase 3 Combat: at least one unit required.

grades.reason: Computes 11 strength, zero after final unit removal, and unit requirement for Combat Intrigue.

grades.question: If you pass Combat Intrigue and an opponent then plays one, may you act again? When does the window close, and where do troops and sandworms go after rewards?
grades.expected: May act again after earlier pass; closes only when all involved players pass consecutively. Adjust strength for effects. After all rewards troops return to supply not garrison, sandworms to bank, Combat markers reset zero.

observed.answer: Yes. Passing does not bar a later play; the window closes after all players involved pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison), sandworms to the bank, and Combat markers reset to 0.
observed.evidence: Phase 3 Combat: may play or pass; consecutive-pass close; cleanup destinations and marker reset.

grades.reason: Allows another play after passing, consecutive-pass closure, and correct postreward destinations/reset.

grades.question: Compare two players tied for first in a four-player Conflict with the same tie in a three-player Conflict. Who takes the Conflict card, and can a zero-strength player get a reward?
grades.expected: Each tied first gets second reward and nobody wins or takes card. In four-player game remaining players compete for third; in three-player game no further rewards. Zero strength never rewarded.

observed.answer: In 4P, the two tied for first each take the second reward; the remaining players compete for the third reward. Nobody wins the Conflict, so nobody takes its card. In 3P, the two tied for first each take the second reward and nobody else is rewarded. A zero-strength player receives no reward.
observed.evidence: Phase 3 Combat—Resolve Combat and Combat ties: tie for first by player count; 0 strength gets none.

grades.reason: Gives both player-count tie branches, no winner/card, and no zero-strength reward.

grades.question: What does a sandworm do to rewards: do two sandworms quadruple them, can control or battle icons double, and how is a reward offering 3 spice for 1 VP handled?
grades.expected: One or more sandworms doubles, never quadruples. Control and battle icons do not double. Optional reward cost may be paid second time: 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 for 2, not free second VP.

observed.answer: One or more sandworms double rewards once; two do not quadruple them. Control of a location and battle icons on a won Conflict card do not double. For an optional 3-spice-for-1-VP reward, you may pay another 3 spice to take it again (6 total spice for 2 VP).
observed.evidence: Actions—Sandworm Reward Doubling: one-or-more, exclusions, and pay cost a second time.

grades.reason: Doubles once for any positive sandworm count, excludes control/icons, and pays twice for two optional VP.

grades.question: When is a normal battle-icon match checked, which cards qualify, is matching optional, and how is a wild icon used?
grades.expected: After winning and taking Conflict card face up in supply check another face-up Conflict or Objective with same icon; must flip pair face down for 1 VP. At Endgame wild can match any of three icons in supply, pair flipped for 1 VP.

observed.answer: After winning and taking the Conflict card face up into your supply, check it against any face-up Conflict or Objective card in your supply. A matching pair must be flipped face down for 1 VP. During Endgame, a wild icon can match any one of the three icons in your supply; flip the pair for 1 VP.
observed.evidence: Actions—Battle Icons: mandatory match after taking card; eligible cards; Endgame wild.

grades.reason: Specifies postwin face-up-card check, eligible Conflict/Objective, mandatory flip for 1 VP, and Endgame wild matching.

grades.question: What are the rewards and reversibility at 2 and 4 Faction Influence, and does tying the Alliance holder at 4 steal the Alliance?
grades.expected: Reach 2 gets 1 VP lost below 2. Reach 4 gets track bonus retained if falling below, can earn again on re-reaching. First to 4 gets Alliance and its VP; tie does not steal, opponent must rise higher. Transfer loses old holder VP and gives new holder VP.

observed.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP and lose that VP below 2; regain it on reaching 2 again. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, keep it if you fall below 4, and earn it again on returning to 4. The first player to 4 also gains the Alliance and 1 VP, which is retained only while holding it. Tying the current holder does not take the Alliance; rise above them. FAQ also says a holder losing Influence after a tie triggers a transfer to a formerly tied opponent.
observed.evidence: Scoring—Faction Influence and FAQ—Alliance loss.

grades.reason: Distinguishes reversible 2-Influence VP, retained/re-earned 4-track bonus, token-linked Alliance VP, and tie versus overtaking; holder-loss exception is also consistent.

grades.question: When can Persuasion be spent during Reveal, may it be pooled or split, can you buy a Row replacement immediately, and where does the acquired card go?
grades.expected: Before between or after Reveal effects; can pool and split. Refill Row to five immediately; may buy replacement with remaining Persuasion. Acquired card face-up discard, cannot use immediately; unspent Persuasion lost.

observed.answer: During Reveal, Persuasion may be spent before, between, or after Reveal effects, including pooled across sources for one card or split across cards. Acquire from the five-card Imperium Row or either Reserve pile; costs are at the top right. The Row refills to five immediately, so its replacement may also be bought if affordable. Acquired cards go face up to your discard pile.
observed.evidence: Actions—Acquiring Cards; Reveal Turn effects.

grades.reason: Allows purchases before/between/after Reveal effects, pooling/splitting, immediate replacement purchase, and face-up discard destination.

grades.question: How do Maker bonus spice, the Shield Wall and Maker Hooks affect harvesting and summoning, and where can a sandworm be placed?
grades.expected: Makers phase adds one bonus spice on each unoccupied Maker space, accumulating; visiting collects all bonus spice. Shield Wall blocks worms at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, Imperial Basin until removed to box. Maker Hooks prerequisite when specified; summoning directly bank to Conflict, never garrison.

observed.answer: An unoccupied Maker space gets 1 bank spice at each Makers phase, accumulating with existing bonus spice; visiting it collects all bonus spice. Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Hooks, two worms; Hagga costs 1 water and offers 2 spice or, with Hooks, one worm. The Shield Wall blocks summoning at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery and Imperial Basin until removed. Worms go directly to your Conflict quadrant, never a garrison; Hooks are retained, not spent, and are not universally required unless the effect says so.
observed.evidence: Phase 4 Makers; Actions—Sandworms; Special Rules—Shield Wall; board-space table.

grades.reason: Covers accumulating/collected Maker spice, stated Hooks/Wall restrictions and protected locations, and direct Conflict deployment rather than garrison.

grades.question: At what point does 10 VP or an empty Conflict deck end play, what happens before comparing final VP, and what are the rulebook resource tiebreakers?
grades.expected: Check in Recall at end of round, not immediately at 10 VP. Resolve Endgame Intrigue first then highest VP wins. Ties spice then Solari then water then garrisoned troops.

observed.answer: At Recall, after a round, 10+ VP by any player or an empty Conflict Deck triggers Endgame. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues, then compare VP. Rulebook tiebreakers are spice, then Solari, water, and garrisoned troops.
observed.evidence: Phase 5 Recall; Scoring / Victory Conditions.

grades.reason: Checks end condition at Recall, resolves Endgame Intrigues before VP comparison, and lists all four resource tiebreakers in order.

grades.question: With optional standard CHOAM, how many contracts start face up and face down, which extra cards are added, is Shaddam compulsory, and are the 10 contrasting-back contracts part of this standard setup?
grades.expected: 20 standard contracts: two face up, eighteen in bank. Add four Intrigue and four Imperium; Shaddam optional. Ten contrasting-back contracts are only Rise of Ix compatibility, excluded from standard setup.

observed.answer: Standard CHOAM starts with two contracts face up and the remaining standard tokens face down in the bank (18 if Shaddam is not chosen; 16 if he is chosen, plus two reserved Sardaukar contracts). Shuffle the four added Intrigues into that deck and four added Imperium cards into that deck. Shaddam is optional. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts stay in the box; they are not part of standard CHOAM.
observed.evidence: CHOAM Module—Setup changes; 10 contrasting-back contracts.

grades.reason: Provides two face-up contracts, 18 in bank ordinarily or correct Shaddam reservation variant, four cards in each deck, optional Leader, and excludes Ix set.

grades.question: Under CHOAM, what does the contract icon do, what if all contracts are taken, and how are Harvest, Immediate and Acquire The Spice Must Flow contracts completed?
grades.expected: With CHOAM, take one of the available face-up contracts on the board into your supply, then replace it face up from the bank if a bank contract remains. The printed icon guide gives 2 Solari if there are none left; this does not require every contract token in the game to have been acquired. In particular, another human with no public contract available gains 2 Solari even if Shaddam's set-aside Sardaukar contracts remain unacquired, and cannot take those reserved contracts. Without CHOAM the icon also gives 2 Solari. Shaddam's own reserved-contract option follows Sardaukar Commander and the FAQ. A Harvest contract completes by sending an Agent to a Maker space and gaining the specified total spice during that turn, including other sources. Immediate completes as soon as taken. Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when that card is next acquired.
grades.source_references: See benchmark-v17/source-reference-appendix.json: original main PDF pp16,20, Uprising Board Space Guide, original Shaddam Leader and official FAQ p3, exact named-file/hash locators.

observed.answer: With CHOAM, the icon takes an available public face-up contract into your supply and refills the offer face up from the bank if possible; if no public offer remains, gain 2 Solari. Harvest completes by visiting a Maker space and gaining at least the specified total spice during that turn; Immediate completes when taken; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
observed.evidence: CHOAM Module—Taking contracts and Completing contracts; Board Space Guide shared contract rule.

grades.reason: Explains public acquisition/refill and 2-Solari exhaustion fallback, Maker-visit total-spice Harvest timing, immediate completion, and next Spice Must Flow acquisition.

grades.question: You gain a board-space contract after already sending your Agent to that space this turn. Can you complete it now? Once completed what do you announce, gain and do with the token?
grades.expected: Cannot complete now; must have held contract when Agent sent, wait future turn. Announce completion, gain printed rewards, flip face down and leave in supply.

observed.answer: No. If you acquire a contract for the space after already sending your Agent there that turn, it must wait until a future turn because you had to hold it when sending the Agent. On completion, announce it, gain its shown rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
observed.evidence: CHOAM Module—Completing contracts.

grades.reason: Rejects retroactive contract completion and states announcement, rewards, face-down flip, and retention in supply.

grades.question: In standard two-player play how many Rivals are used, who gets the Ornithopter Objective, who gets First Player, what is the turn order, and does a Rival Reveal?
grades.expected: One shared Rival. Rival gets Ornithopter Objective, other two randomly humans; Rival never First Player. Marker alternates humans, Rival considered clockwise from First Player and acts between humans each round. Takes Agent turns while it has Agent in supply, never Reveals.

observed.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as third competitor. The Rival gets the Ornithopter Objective; First Player is the human whose Objective bears the marker, and alternates only between the humans. Turn order is First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival never Reveals.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup; Agent turns; Player Turns.

grades.reason: Gives one shared Rival, its Ornithopter Objective, marker-bearing human First Player, human/Rival/human order, and no Rival Reveal.

grades.question: A Rival reveals an occupied board space, then a Place Spy card. How does it proceed, which space costs and effects apply, and what happens when House Hagal is empty or Reshuffle is drawn?
grades.expected: Occupied: ignore and reveal again. Place Spy tries empty designated post, ignore placement if none, then reveal another card regardless because no Agent sent. Ignore normal space costs/effects; use Hagal effects only. Empty deck or Reshuffle: immediately reshuffle Hagal and continue.

observed.answer: For an occupied destination, ignore it and reveal another Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: place a Spy at an empty post of the specified type if possible, otherwise ignore placement; in either case reveal another card and continue the same Agent turn. Ignore normal space costs/effects and apply only Hagal effects. If the deck empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Agent turns and Place Spy cards.

grades.reason: Handles occupied destination, successful/failed Place Spy followed by another draw, Hagal-only effects/cost exemption, and immediate reshuffle.

grades.question: How are eligible Objective cards selected and distributed in standard three- or four-player setup, how is First Player chosen, and may Shaddam be chosen without CHOAM?
grades.expected: Omit Objectives whose 1–3P or 4/6P mark mismatches count; shuffle, each takes one random face up in supply. First Player is holder of marked Objective. Shaddam cannot be chosen without CHOAM.

observed.answer: For 3–4 players, shuffle Objectives after removing cards whose 1-3P/4/6P marking does not match, then give each player one random face-up Objective; its First Player marker identifies the first player. Shaddam may be used only with the CHOAM Module, so not without it.
observed.evidence: Setup steps 3 and 5; Shaddam setup; scope.

grades.reason: Removes count-ineligible Objectives, randomizes/deals face-up cards, selects marked holder, and bars Shaddam without CHOAM.

grades.question: If the bank runs out of Solari, spice, water or sandworms, what happens? Contrast an empty personal troop supply, and state where resource payments go.
grades.expected: Bank resources and sandworms not limited; substitute conveniently. Cannot recruit troops from empty personal supply until returned. Resource gains come from bank and payments return to bank.

observed.answer: Bank resources are not limited: make convenient substitutions if Solari, spice, water, or sandworms run out. An empty personal troop supply means you cannot recruit more until troops return there. Gains come from the bank and payments return to it.
observed.evidence: Setup step 7; Recruiting & Deploying Units.

grades.reason: Allows substitutes for all bank resources/sandworms, distinguishes limited troop supply, and returns payments to bank.

grades.question: State all five round phases in order, when Conflict and hand cards are drawn, and what Recall does if Endgame is not triggered.
grades.expected: Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. Start reveals top Conflict face up atop previous remaining cards then each draws five. If no Endgame, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise and begin next round (two-player Rival exception).

observed.answer: The phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal a Conflict first, resolve any control defensive troop, then each player draws five cards. If Recall does not trigger Endgame, humans return Agents to Leaders; pass First Player clockwise in 3–4P, or return Rival Agents to supply and pass the marker to the other human in 2P; start the next round.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure: five phases; Phase 1 and Phase 5.

grades.reason: States all five phases in order, Round Start Conflict-then-five draw, and Recall Agent/First Player reset including Rival exception.

grades.question: May you resolve board-space effects, Agent-box effects and Faction Influence in any order? Can you use that visit’s Influence to meet its entry requirement?
grades.expected: Resolve effects in any order after placement, but entry requirements and costs must be met before any effects. Cannot rely on Influence gained by the visit for its entry requirement.

observed.answer: Yes, you may resolve space effects, Agent-box effects, and other effects in any order. But entry requirements and costs must be met before effects resolve, so the visit’s Influence gain cannot satisfy its own entry requirement.
observed.evidence: Agent Turn: pay/meet requirements first; effects may be in any order. Board Space Guide.

grades.reason: Allows effect ordering while rejecting use of postentry Influence to meet entry requirements.

grades.question: Can an optional arrow cost be paid twice in an Agent turn? Which effects are normally optional or mandatory, including costs on Intrigue cards?
grades.expected: Only once per turn, except sandworm-doubled Conflict rewards. Most effects mandatory except may, optional arrow payment and black-X trash. Direct self-trash mandatory. All Intrigue conditions/costs required to play it.
grades.source_references: Main pp9,20; FAQ p3 optional effects/paying a cost

observed.answer: No. An arrow cost/effect may be used only once per turn, with the exception of sandworm doubling a Conflict reward. Most card and space effects are mandatory; “may,” optional arrow costs, and the black-X trash icon are optional. Intrigue conditions and costs must be met to play it.
observed.evidence: Special Rules—Arrows / paying costs; FAQ—Mandatory effects and costs.

grades.reason: Gives once-per-turn optional-arrow limit with doubled-Conflict exception, ordinary mandatory effects and named optional categories, and mandatory Intrigue costs/conditions.

grades.question: Where may a new Spy be placed, what if all your Spies are already deployed, and what if its placement effect specifies an Agent-icon type?
grades.expected: Unoccupied observation post, from supply. If none in supply may first recall one of own Spies for no effect. Specified icon must connect to post or cannot place there.

observed.answer: A Spy icon normally places a Spy from supply on an unoccupied observation post (subject to any specified connected Agent icon type). If you have none in supply, you may first recall one of your Spies for no effect. If the placement effect specifies an Agent icon that must connect to the post, use only such a post or placement is not possible.
observed.evidence: Special Rules—Spies & observation posts.

grades.reason: Gives unoccupied-post placement from supply, free no-effect recall if all deployed, and required connection to any specified Agent-icon type.

grades.question: Can you Infiltrate your own occupied board space, use a Spy without playing a card, or recall two connected Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement?
grades.expected: No to all. Infiltrate bypasses another player Agent; still play a card and meet entry costs/requirements. Two Spies can pay different effects (Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence), not duplicate Gather Intelligence.

observed.answer: No: Infiltrate only bypasses another player’s Agent, not your own. A Spy action does not replace the required played card for an Agent turn. You cannot recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on the same placement; you may use two for different effects, one Infiltrate and one Gather Intelligence.
observed.evidence: Special Rules—Spies; FAQ—Spies.

grades.reason: Rejects all three proposed uses, preserves required Agent-turn card, and permits only different-effect double recalls.

grades.question: Who gets control bonuses when visiting Arrakeen, Spice Refinery or Imperial Basin, how is control transferred, and where does the defensive troop originate?
grades.expected: Winning respective Conflict puts control marker on flag replacing opponent. Controller receives 1 Solari at Arrakeen/Refinery or 1 spice at Basin whenever anyone including self visits. Reveal of controlled location Conflict permits one troop from supply directly to Conflict.

observed.answer: At controlled Arrakeen and Spice Refinery, the controller gets 1 Solari whenever anyone visits; at Imperial Basin the controller gets 1 spice. Winning the named Conflict gives control, placing your marker and replacing an opponent’s. When a revealed Conflict is at a space you already control, deploy one defensive troop from your supply directly to Conflict, without an Agent visit.
observed.evidence: Special Rules—Critical Locations & Control; Round Start.

grades.reason: Identifies controller, exact location bonuses on any visit, winning-Conflict control replacement, and supply-origin defensive deployment at reveal.

grades.question: When two players tie for second in a three-player Conflict, what happens? What if players tie for third in four-player play, or three players tie for first?
grades.expected: Tied second each get third reward; winner keeps first and card, no other rewards. Tied third receive nothing. Three tied first each get second, no winner/card and no further rewards.

observed.answer: In a 3P tie for second, each tied player gets the third reward; the Conflict winner keeps first reward and card, with no further rewards. Tied for third get nothing. Three tied for first each get the second reward; nobody wins or takes the card, and no other reward is given even in 4P.
observed.evidence: Special Rules—Combat ties and three tied for first.

grades.reason: Covers second-tie third rewards with winner retained, no third-tie reward, and three-first-tie second rewards without winner/card or further rewards.

grades.question: At a normal three-player Conflict with three different positive strengths, which places receive rewards? What if a two-player game’s Rival is one of the participants?
grades.expected: Only first and second rewarded, third only used for a tie for second. Two humans plus standard Rival use the same two-/three-player reward rules; Rival competes normally.
grades.source_references: Main p14; Supplements p5 Combat; FAQ p1 Conflict

observed.answer: In a normal 3P Conflict with three distinct positive strengths, first and second receive their rewards; third receives nothing. This is also true with a two-human game’s Rival, since the Rival counts as the third competitor. The printed third reward in games of 2–3 players is used only for a tie for second.
observed.evidence: Phase 3—Resolve Combat: player-count reward ranks.

grades.reason: Pays only distinct first and second in three-player Combat and applies the same rule with a Rival.

grades.question: When can Plot, Combat and Endgame Intrigues be played, how are unplayed Intrigues kept and ordinary ones discarded, and what if the Intrigue deck is exhausted?
grades.expected: Plot during own Agent/Reveal turns, Combat during Combat with a unit, Endgame at game end. Unplayed face down separate from deck, owner may inspect; played resolved cards face up Intrigue discard. Exhaustion reshuffles Intrigue discard into new deck.
grades.source_references: Main p7 / extraction 345–354; FAQ p2 Intrigue cards

observed.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played on your Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues during Combat only if you have a unit in Conflict; Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep Intrigues face down, separate from your deck, and reveal only when playing; after resolving, put them face up in the Intrigue discard pile. If the Intrigue deck runs out, shuffle its discard into a new deck.
observed.evidence: Special Rules—Intrigue cards; FAQ—Draw timing.

grades.reason: Gives own-turn Plot, unit-gated Combat, and Endgame timing, face-down separate storage, face-up postresolution discard, and exhaustion reshuffle.

grades.question: Can you discard an Intrigue for an ordinary discard instruction? Where does an ordinary discard come from? How does Secrets choose which Intrigue is stolen?
grades.expected: Ordinary discard from hand and cannot be Intrigue unless specified. Secrets steals one random Intrigue from each opponent with four or more, in addition to drawing one from deck and gaining Bene Gesserit Influence.
grades.source_references: Main p20 / extraction 1104–1106,1179–1181; Supplements p2; FAQ p2 discard

observed.answer: An ordinary discard is a card of your choice from your hand and cannot be an Intrigue unless specified. The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. Secrets gives you one Intrigue selected at random from each opponent who has at least four Intrigues.
observed.evidence: Special Rules—Discarding; Intrigue cards.

grades.reason: Restricts ordinary discard to hand/non-Intrigue unless specified and correctly selects one random Intrigue from each 4+-Intrigue opponent.

grades.question: Which cards may a trash effect remove, where do ordinary and Reserve cards go, and is trashing optional? Does trashing The Spice Must Flow remove its acquired VP?
grades.expected: May trash own hand, discard or in-play card. Ordinary to box; Reserve back to its Reserve stack. Optional unless cost or direct self-trash. The Spice Must Flow acquire VP retained after trashing.
grades.source_references: Main p20 / extraction 1185–1190; FAQ p4 The Spice Must Flow

observed.answer: Trash effects may remove cards from your hand, discard pile, or in play. Return ordinary trashed cards to the box; Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless paying a cost or directed to trash itself. The Spice Must Flow’s acquired VP remains even if the card is later trashed.
observed.evidence: Actions—Trashing; FAQ—Victory.

grades.reason: Covers hand/discard/in-play trashing, box versus Reserve destinations, optionality exceptions, and persistent Spice Must Flow acquire VP.

grades.question: When do acquire-box effects resolve, when do you reshuffle your deck, and can unused Persuasion be carried to another round?
grades.expected: Acquire effect once at acquisition not when later played. Reshuffle discard only when unable to draw due to empty deck then continue. Unspent Reveal Persuasion lost, never saved.

observed.answer: Acquire-box effects resolve once at the moment you acquire the card. If your deck is empty when you need to draw, shuffle your discard into a new deck and continue. Unused Persuasion is lost at end of Reveal; it cannot carry over.
observed.evidence: Special Rules—Acquire box; Actions—Acquiring Cards.

grades.reason: Places acquire trigger at acquisition, reshuffles only when a draw needs an empty deck, and loses unused Persuasion.

grades.question: What counts as in play for Fremen Bond, can two Bond cards activate one another regardless of play order, and when do they cease being in play?
grades.expected: Agent-turn and Reveal cards remain in play face up until Reveal Clean Up unless trashed earlier. Bond requires at least one other Fremen in play; two Bond cards can activate each other regardless of order.

observed.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and revealed on Reveal remain face up and in play until Clean Up (unless trashed first). Fremen Bond can use one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards can activate each other regardless of order. They cease to be in play when moved to discard at Clean Up.
observed.evidence: Special Rules—In play / Fremen Bond.

grades.question: What do Arrakeen, Fremkit and Research Station each cost and provide, what Agent icons access them, and which are Combat spaces?

grades.question: How do High Council’s first and subsequent visits differ, what does each cost, when is its ongoing benefit used, and is it a Combat space?
